title.narrative: Education and WASH integrated life-saving, life-sustaining, and resilience-based assistance in the underserved communities of Aleppo and Deir-Ez-Zor (Priority 1 and 2)

description.narrative: ltpgtIn line with the Strategic Priorities 1 and 2 of SHF's 1st SA of 2024, WW-GVC aims to carry out a multi-sectoral integrated life-saving, life-sustaining and resilience-based assistance primarily focused on the Education and WASH sectors in Aleppo and Deir Ez Zor. The objective of the project is to enhance the delivery of basic, critical, and quality WASH and Education services for vulnerable populations affected by the Syrian crisis in the underserved areas of Aleppo and Deir Ez Zor. Protection, AAP, GBV and PSEA prevention will be key cross-cutting approaches throughout the whole action. The project will reach a total of 321,700 unique beneficiaries. In summary:ltbrgtltbgtEducation: lt/bgtThe project will increase access to safe, quality, and protective education services in underserved areas of Aleppo and Deir Ez Zor. Under Priority 2, access will be increased through the light rehabilitation and minor repair of 26 classrooms with their respective WASH facilities, provision of essential school furniture and solar powered systems, and the distribution of school supplies. While in terms of quality, the project will train 10 Educational Guidance as trainers, support the professional development of 150 teachers, activate NFE programs (remedial education) to 1,500 children, provide school supplies to 3,000 children, and provide both teachers and students with PSS. The Education result will reach a total of 150 teachers, 10 Educational Guidance, and 3,000 children. Additionally, under Priority 1, the project aims to support 300 crossline students who plan to present at the national exams GoS areas. The support will focus on the provision of WASH NFIs, Stationery, and Educational Support while they stay in accommodation centers.ltbrgtltbgtWASH: lt/bgtThe project will improve access to safe, reliable, and sustainable Water and Sanitation services for the same targeted communities of the Education. The intervention will not only ensure access to water and sanitation to the communities but also to the schools. The project's logic is divided into both priorities of SHF's SA. Under Priority 1, this will be achieved through an emergency intervention restoring efficient functionality of Tishreen Pumping Station in Aleppo, in addition to the emergency repair of water networks in Aleppo city. Morevover, with the intervention on the water networks in Abo Jrin, Aqrabuz, and Abo Dreikha in As-Safira Subdistrict of Aleppo, combined with the minor repair of their connected water reservoirs, increasing water storage and therefore the whole efficiency of the system. In Deir Ez Zor city, the project will focus on emergency spot repair of wastewater networks in the overcrowded neighborhoods at risk of public health hazards in Al Joura and Al Qusour. In total, 321,700 direct beneficiaries, and 1,232,960 indirect beneficiaries will be reached.ltbrgtThe response under both sectors will be integrated in the same priority locations of the call and reaching the same beneficiaries according to the needs. Additionally, the proposed project intends to complement other interventions implemented by WW-GVC and funded by ECHO and AICS, maximizing impact and resource mobilization under WW-GVC’s area-based approach. Moreover, projects carried out in by other humanitarian actors in the same geographic areas will also be complemented. The activities proposed are in line with the result of a rapid and detailed needs assessment conducted by WW-GVC in the targeted locations (see Annex 1). The coordination with all relevant stakeholders including MoE, MoWR, and both the WASH and Educations sectors was completed during the proposal development and their endorsement of the proposal was obtained.ltbrgtIn terms of budget, the total project's budget isnbsp975,044.80 USD of whichnbsp925,044.80 USD requested from SHF.lt/pgt
